summary: Marion County, TN tower; register dates it to the 1930s and ties it to the new Prentice Cooper State Forest; NHLR-registered 2017, listed as standing; no exact build year or staffing found.

facts.height_note: NHLR gives no height. A TN Division of Forestry weather station on Walden's Ridge (1,920 ft) describes a 100 ft fire tower just west of its equipment but does not name it; not confirmed as this tower

access.note: No visiting rules or climbing permission for this tower are in the sources read; the Clio entry says the state forest is often closed for deer and turkey hunts; tnlandforms advises against climbing the towers

visit.trail_note: Forest has more than 30 miles of hiking trails; it is often closed for deer and turkey hunts, so check before visiting

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the tower to the 1930s and ties it to the newly formed forest, but the state's forest land purchases began in 1938 and the forest was dedicated in 1945; no source gives an exact build year, so the story gives only the decade

sources.title: Prentice Cooper State Forest and Wildlife Management Area

notes_for_editor: Build year is only the decade '1930s' (NHLR); no exact year found, so no 'built' event is recorded. The 100-foot tower comes from the NWS station description: the station sits on Walden's Ridge at 1,920 ft, the same elevation the NHLR gives for this tower, but the NWS page does not name the tower, so height_m is null and the story does not assert the match. The NHLR record does not place the tower inside the forest, so that phrase was dropped. Forest history is from Clio, a community encyclopedia, not the state; the tn.gov forest page refused the connection twice and was not read. Searches suggested CCC work at other Tennessee towers but no source ties the CCC to this tower, so none is claimed. Current condition rests on the tnlandforms 'standing' mark and the NWS station's present-tense description.
